Each f_i is homogeneous in S with weighted degree deg(f_i)=A+i

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Let A,B,d ∈ Z with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, and define Q_{A,B,d}(q)=∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) with Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1. If Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q], then in the weighted graded polynomial ring S=Q[x_1,...,x_d] (or S=Q if d=0) with deg(x_i)=B+i, there exist homogeneous elements f_1,...,f_d ∈ S such that deg(f_i)=A+i for each i=1..d and for each i the class of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor (so f_1,...,f_d form a homogeneous regular sequence). Consequently, the graded data of S modulo this regular sequence yields the given expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) (as stated in the equivalence).

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
Let M_j := S/(g_1,...,g_j) for 0 <= j <= d; in particular M_0 = S. Because each g_i is homogeneous, each ideal (g_1,...,g_j) is homogeneous, so each M_j inherits a positive grading, and each (M_j)_n is finite-dimensional over k as a quotient of S_n.

First compute Hilb_S(q). The monomials x_1^(a_1)...x_d^(a_d) form a k-basis of S, and such a monomial has degree a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d. Hence S_n has basis consisting of the monomials with a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d = n. Because every w_i is positive, each a_i is bounded by n/w_i, so only finitely many tuples (a_1,...,a_d) occur for a fixed n. Therefore
Hilb_S(q) = sum_{a_1,...,a_d >= 0} q^(a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d)
= prod_{i=1}^d (sum_{m >= 0} q^(m w_i))
= prod_{i=1}^d 1/(1 - q^(w_i)),
as a formal power series; the Cauchy product is legitimate because for each degree n only finitely many tuples contribute. When d = 0, this says Hilb_S(q) = 1, which is true because then S = k.

Now fix j with 1 <= j <= d, and write e_j = deg(g_j). Since g_1,...,g_d is a regular sequence, the class of g_j in M_{j-1} is not a zero-divisor. Thus multiplication by g_j on M_{j-1} is injective. Because g_j is homogeneous of degree e_j, for every n >= 0 we obtain an injective k-linear map
mu_{j,n} : (M_{j-1})_{n-e_j} -> (M_{j-1})_n,   m -> g_j m,
where we interpret (M_{j-1})_t as 0 for t < 0.

Its image is exactly the degree-n part of g_j M_{j-1}. Indeed, if y is a homogeneous element of degree n in g_j M_{j-1}, write y = g_j m and decompose m = sum_r m_r into homogeneous parts. Then y = sum_r g_j m_r, and each g_j m_r is homogeneous of degree r + e_j. Since y itself has degree n, all terms except the one with r = n - e_j must be zero; hence y = g_j m_{n-e_j}. So
(g_j M_{j-1})_n = g_j (M_{j-1})_{n-e_j} = im(mu_{j,n}).
Because g_j M_{j-1} is homogeneous and M_j = M_{j-1}/g_j M_{j-1} = S/(g_1,...,g_j), we have
(M_j)_n = (M_{j-1})_n / (g_j M_{j-1})_n.
Combining this with the description of the image of mu_{j,n} gives a short exact sequence
0 -> (M_{j-1})_{n-e_j} -> (M_{j-1})_n -> (M_j)_n -> 0
for every n >= 0.

Let a_n^(j) := dim_k (M_j)_n, and set a_t^(j-1) := 0 for t < 0. Taking dimensions in the short exact sequence yields
a_n^(j) = a_n^(j-1) - a_{n-e_j}^(j-1).
Multiplying by q^n and summing over n >= 0, we get
Hilb_{M_j}(q)
= sum_{n >= 0} a_n^(j) q^n
= sum_{n >= 0} (a_n^(j-1) - a_{n-e_j}^(j-1)) q^n
= Hilb_{M_{j-1}}(q) - q^(e_j) Hilb_{M_{j-1}}(q)
= (1 - q^(e_j)) Hilb_{M_{j-1}}(q).

Applying this successively for j = 1,2,...,d, we obtain
Hilb_{S/(g_1,...,g_d)}(q) = Hilb_{M_d}(q)
= (prod_{j=1}^d (1 - q^(e_j))) Hilb_S(q)
= prod_{j=1}^d (1 - q^(e_j)) / prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(w_i)).
This is exactly the claimed formula. For d = 0 there are no g_i, so M_d = S = k and both products are empty, hence equal to 1, and the same formula gives Hilb_k(q) = 1.

payload.statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. For a positively graded k-algebra R = direct_sum_{n >= 0} R_n, write Hilb_R(q) := sum_{n >= 0} (dim_k R_n) q^n. If g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S and deg(g_i)=e_i for each i, then Hilb_{S/(g_1,...,g_d)}(q) = prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(e_i)) / prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(w_i)), with the empty product interpreted as 1 when d=0.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof explicitly justifies finiteness of each graded piece of S and hence of each M_j, so the Hilbert series manipulations are legitimate.
The key exactness step is established componentwise using that multiplication by g_j is injective on M_{j-1} and that g_j M_{j-1} is a homogeneous submodule.
No semantic drift from the lemma statement or the root theorem sketch was detected; this is the intended Hilbert-series computation needed for the assembly.

result_payload.reason: The proof correctly computes the Hilbert series of a weighted polynomial ring and then uses the regular-sequence hypothesis to derive the standard short exact sequence on graded pieces, yielding Hilb_{M_j}(q) = (1-q^{e_j}) Hilb_{M_{j-1}}(q). Iterating gives the claimed product formula, and the d=0 case is handled. The argument matches the lemma sketch and role in the assembly with no substantive semantic drift.
